answer: At the inlet of each epoch, every identity seals a salt-keyed, memory-hard replica of a public dataset and commits its trellis of Merkle roots before the audit seed appears. A quill-signed receipt records random blocks returned within seconds; missing or mismatched blocks void reward and slash that identity's escrow. The farm's cheapest move is one shared master with salted blocks rebuilt on demand, but each block depends on the whole slow seal: every extra clone pays a non-poolable cost of one live replica and separately locked escrow. If either is skipped, its audit fails.
